answer: Each agent claims one cedar pole pair and locks a 70-credit bond. A thread strung between the poles is key-signed to that agent, which reports midspan sag plus a zephyr wind log. An auditor recomputes expected sag from the public cedar span and thread tension tables and the filed zephyr log, burning the bond on mismatch or reuse. The first claim pays 37; the kth pays 37+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5032 and 1,000 fakes cost 2,534,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-pole ring fails: one thread carries one key, so copied sag diverges. An honest agent pays 37 once, bond back after a clean audit.
